claim: Raising 30 kg/h of feed water at 15 C to dry saturated steam takes 21.78 kW
law: Steady-flow energy equation; latent heat 2.257 MJ/kg at 1.013 bar (steam tables)
check: claimed 21.7783 kW, estimate 21.8 kW (ratio 1.00)

claim: Fuel energy 32.9 kW = heat to water + stack + shell + unburned losses
law: First law over the firebox, bank, economizer and chimney
check: in 32.94 kW, out 32.94 kW

claim: Fuel-to-steam efficiency 66.1 % stays below the first-law ceiling set by the unburned loss alone
law: First law: efficiency <= 1 - unburned fraction (stack at ambient, no shell loss)

claim: The coil takes 17.5 kW (16.6 kW/m2) from firebox gas at 519 C
law: Radiant exchange sigma F (Tg^4 - Tw^4) with F = 0.40, plus convection at 20 W/(m2 K); the flux may not exceed black-body exchange plus the same convection

claim: Exchange factor F = 0.40 and coil convection 20 W/(m2 K) in a hand-fed firebox (efficiency 63.8 to 68.3 % for F = 0.25 to 0.60)
law: Well-stirred zone model of a firebox (Hottel zone method, single zone); F and h set by flame luminosity and plume velocity, not calculable from first principles at TRL 3
check: R5 (65 %) is met for F 0.40 to 0.60 at lambda 1.5 and missed at F 0.25 (STR-CAL-001 v0.5 Table 6); the correlation at the mean firebox velocity gives about 9 W/(m2 K), not 20 (independent review), worth about 2.6 points; flue temperature and oxygen to be measured

claim: Bank gas-side coefficient 24.0 W/(m2 K) clean, 22.4 with fouling, gas crossing the tubes at 1.04 m/s (gas-pass baffle, 10 % edge bypass)
law: Zukauskas in-line bank correlation with the row factor per pass (CAL) checked against Hilpert's single-cylinder correlation Nu = 0.683 Re^0.466 Pr^1/3 with the same row factor and gas radiation (same correlation family, so a consistency check, not an independent one)
check: claimed 24.0305 W/(m2 K), estimate 26.2 W/(m2 K) (ratio 0.92)
closed_by: STR-DEC-001 S1 (gas-pass baffles, 2026-10-24); STR-CAL-001 v0.5 section 4

claim: Economizer gas-side coefficient 23.0 W/(m2 K) clean, 21.5 with fouling, three baffled passes at 0.7 to 1.0 m/s
law: As S6, middle pass
check: claimed 22.9508 W/(m2 K), estimate 28.2 W/(m2 K) (ratio 0.81)
closed_by: STR-DEC-001 S1 (gas-pass baffles, 2026-10-24); STR-CAL-001 v0.5 section 4

claim: Firebox outer skin 99 C behind 50 mm of ceramic fibre (about 135 C if the hot face near the fire bed is 700 C)
law: Series conduction and outside film: k 0.12 W/(m K), h 12 W/(m2 K); the skin must stay below the gas temperature and is a burn hazard above 60 C (no requirement limits it yet; DEC #21)

claim: The steam front must reach 16.5 cm so that 15 cm stays at 70 C through a 25 min hold
law: Two semi-infinite bodies in contact: the interface sits at the mean temperature and the profile follows erf(x / 2 sqrt(alpha t))
check: claimed 1.53403 cm of overshoot, estimate 1.53 cm of overshoot (ratio 1.00)

claim: Heating 16.5 cm of moist soil by 85 K takes 30.6 MJ/m2
law: Q = rho c dT V with c = 0.84 + 0.20 x 4.18 kJ/(kg K) for 20 % water
check: claimed 30.6207 MJ/m2, estimate 30.6 MJ/m2 (ratio 1.00)

claim: Steam passes down through 16.5 cm of soil at full flow without lifting the 256 Pa hood
law: Darcy's law at the superficial steam velocity of 1.16 cm/s; intrinsic permeability 1e-10 (sand) to 1e-12 m2 (loam), textbook ranges, not measured
check: needs 236 Pa in sand, 2,362 Pa in sandy loam, 23,617 Pa in loam against 256 Pa (583 Pa with 40 kg of ballast); holds only in loose sandy soil at full flow (92 % of the lift limit even there); moist soil passes gas less well still, and the 10 % skirt leakage in CAL does not depend on permeability (independent review); fixes (bed preparation, stakes or straps, a deeper skirt, a larger hood or lower steam flux) change how the machine is used, so they go to Amish
closed_by: To Amish (STR-DEC-001 #18); TRL 4 soil tests decided 2026-10-02

claim: Natural draft 16.8 Pa covers the gas-side losses (11.4 Pa, fuel bed included) and the damper openings at lambda 1.5
law: Stack effect g H (rho_air - rho_gas) over 2.50 m at a mean 400 C; losses at the fuel bed (3 Pa, Ergun estimate), holes, baffled passes, chimney and cap; openings at Cd 0.6. Failed with the 2.4 m chimney once the fuel bed was counted (0.1 Pa left)
check: 7531.91 mm2 of opening needed <= 1.26e+04 mm2 of opening needed
closed_by: STR-DEC-001 S3 (chimney outlet 3.2 m); STR-CAL-001 v0.5 section 4

claim: Normal pressure at the bank inlet 0.129 bar, the highest on the steam side, stays within R6
law: Two-phase friction (Muller-Steinhagen and Heck) with a helical coil factor (Ito), acceleration, gravity, hose and manifold losses
check: 0.128831 bar gauge <= 0.15 bar gauge

claim: The water seal blows at 0.084 bar, above the 0.033 bar header pressure
law: Hydrostatics: p = rho g h for the 890 mm dip leg in water at 100 C; the overflow at the static mark removes the annulus rise

claim: The 350 mm overflow loop seal (3,291 Pa) holds against the head-space back pressure of a refeed flash
law: Hydrostatics against the vent pipe's friction and exit loss at the flash flow; the margin is 34 % on pressure, about 16 % on flow, so a flash faster than about 26 s breaks it
check: 3290.67 Pa >= 2453 Pa; the flash basis (30 s, coil at the loaded gas temperature) is not bounded (independent review); to Amish (DEC #20)

claim: The 3/4 in, 15 psi certified valve passes the 141 kg/h dry-coil refeed flash
law: Napier's formula (ASME Section IV practice) and the maker's capacity table, 375 lb/h (Watts Series 315); the valve and seal sit at the header, downstream of the coil where a flash builds about 1.5 bar
check: 170.099 kg/h >= 140.9 kg/h; 21 % margin against an unbounded flash basis; a dry coil hotter than the loaded gas (700 to 800 C) could flash about 2 kg (independent review); to Amish (DEC #20)

claim: A dry coil at 519 C stores 2.73 MJ and flashes 1.17 kg of refeed water
law: Stored heat m c dT of 316 tube (c 0.50 kJ/(kg K)) against latent plus sensible heat of the feed
check: claimed 1.17431 kg, estimate 1.13 kg (ratio 1.04); arithmetic holds, but a dry coil no longer cools the gas and may reach 700 to 800 C (about 2 kg); to Amish with S15 and S16 (DEC #20)

claim: Coil hoop stress at the 3 bar pump shut-off stays far below the yield of 316 at 700 C
law: Thin-wall hoop stress p D / 2t; 316 yield at 700 C about 100 MPa (hot strength, conservative)

claim: Hood handle bar with half of 40 kg of ballast at mid-span and a load factor of 2 stays below yield
law: Simply supported beam M = F L / 4 on a 30 x 30 x 2.5 SHS, Z = 2,330 mm3; S235 yield 235 MPa

claim: Wood at 20 % moisture (wet basis) gives 14.48 MJ/kg lower heating value
law: Channiwala and Parikh correlation for the dry HHV, less the latent heat of the product and fuel water; checked against 19 MJ/kg dry wood LHV
check: claimed 14.4839 MJ/kg, estimate 14.7 MJ/kg (ratio 0.98)

claim: Stoichiometric air 4.76 kg per kg of wet fuel
law: C + O2 -> CO2, 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O, less fuel oxygen; air 23.2 % oxygen by mass
check: claimed 4.75977 kg/kg, estimate 4.76 kg/kg (ratio 1.00)

claim: Flue gas at lambda 1.5 holds 12.5 % water vapour; dew point 51 C, so the cold end of the economizer runs wet
law: Dalton's law and the Antoine equation for water
check: 50.5364 C (dew point above the feed inlet wall) >= 20 C (dew point above the feed inlet wall)
closed_by: STR-CAL-001 v0.5 section 4; stainless tube and 304 baffles (STR-DEC-001 S1)

claim: Wood fires make carbon monoxide, and less excess air raises the CO made
law: Incomplete combustion of carbon (C + 1/2 O2 -> CO) where mixing or temperature is poor; CO is odourless and toxic
check: Firebox and chimney outdoors only, personal CO alarm (PRC safety; RSK H5); the 4 % unburned loss in CAL is an assumption

claim: 316 stainless coil, bank and economizer resist acidic flue condensate and a dry-fire excursion to about 500 C; 304 for the bank baffle and 316L for the economizer baffles
law: Austenitic stainless steels keep a passive chromium oxide film in mildly acidic, chloride-poor condensate and scale slowly below about 800 C
check: Design choice decided by Amish 2026-09-25 (coil); economizer baffles changed from 304 to 316L after the independent review, since wood condensate carries organic acids and chloride and drips onto them; welded 316 sensitizes between about 450 and 850 C in a dry-coil excursion (316L or low-carbon filler to be specified)

claim: Holding soil at 70 C or more for 20 to 30 min kills most weed seeds and soil-borne pathogens
law: Extension guidance: 160 to 180 F (71 to 82 C) for 30 min (Mississippi State University Extension P4033); 140 to 180 F for 30 min for pathogens and weeds (NCAT, 2022)
check: 70 C for 20 to 30 min sits inside both ranges; some hard-seeded weeds survive (accepted in STR-PRS-001 assumptions)

claim: Soil behind the steam front reaches 100 C for most of the hold, more than the 82 C ceiling extension guidance gives
law: MSU P4033: exceeding 180 F (82 C) can harm soil structure; NCAT 2022: overheating kills beneficial nitrifying bacteria
check: Known side effect of steaming with saturated steam; accepted in PRC and carried as risk RSK H9; aerated steam at 70 C to 80 C would avoid it but adds a blower (suggestion in REVIEW)

claim: Condensing steam on skin causes deep burns within about a second
law: Latent heat 2.26 MJ/kg released on contact at 100 C, on top of the sensible heat of hot water
check: Steam diverted to the vent before a hood is lifted; PPE; 5 m exclusion (PRC safety; RSK H1, H2)

claim: One operator lifts and resets a 31.3 kg hood, 1.2 x 1.0 m, by its two side handles 1.12 m apart
law: Revised NIOSH lifting equation (NIOSH 94-110): load constant 23 kg for one person under ideal conditions; the handle span is wider than one person's reach
check: 31.2648 kg <= 23 kg; with the horizontal multiplier for a 1.0 to 1.2 m load the one-person limit is nearer 10 to 14 kg and a two-person share of 15.6 kg is borderline (independent review); fix proposed: a hood wheel kit or lifting aid; changes the one-operator scope, so it goes to Amish (STR-DEC-001 S2)

claim: 15.6 kg of steam per m2 at 15 cm
law: Steam = (soil + hood heat) / latent heat / (1 - skirt leakage)
check: claimed 15.5675 kg/m2, estimate 15.6 kg/m2 (ratio 1.00)

claim: Two hoods treat 1.88 m2/h at 15 cm
law: Rate = steam output / steam per m2 (steam limited), less the vented minute per changeover
check: claimed 1.87686 m2/h, estimate 1.93 m2/h (ratio 0.97); arithmetic holds, but a 4 cm unheated edge strip, overlap between settings and hose and header losses would cut the net rate to about 1.5 to 1.6 m2/h (independent review); to verify at TRL 4

claim: Heated section holds 7.32 L of water flooded
law: Bore area x length for coil, bank, economizer and header

claim: One 125 L fill lasts 4.17 h at 30 kg/h
law: Volume / flow
check: claimed 4.16667 h, estimate 4.17 h (ratio 1.00)

claim: Every efficiency, rate and pressure is a point estimate with a stated band
law: Sensitivity tables in CAL (lambda 1.5 to 2.5, F 0.25 to 0.60, permeability over two decades); correlations about +/- 30 %
check: R5 at risk inside the band; R2 margins under 2 %; carried to RSK

claim: The steam side can never be isolated from the vent: no valve between coil and seal pot, diverter with no closed position
law: Open-vent principle of atmospheric boilers; Texas Health and Safety Code 755.022(a)(4) asks for two independent means to prevent pressure build-up
check: Water seal (first means) and certified relief valve (second means); whether these meet 755.022(a)(4) is for the TDLR ruling (REG R1)

claim: A stalled feed pump can never restart by itself into a hot, dry coil: the coil outlet alarm (about 150 C) latches the pump off until it is reset by hand
law: A dry coil heats at about 17 kW / 6.5 kJ/K = 2.6 K/s, so about 16 to 20 s to 150 C (the 2 to 3 min in the first draft was the time constant); a pump that stalls on low battery and recovers would otherwise refeed it unattended (independent review)
check: Failed as first written (alarm only, wrong timing); fixed by a latching relay with a manual reset (BOM line 16)

claim: The 12 V 20 Ah lead-acid battery runs the feed pump and alarms through one 4.2 h fill
law: Charge = current x time; a diaphragm pump of this class draws a few amperes (ASSUMED 4 A until the pump is chosen); lead-acid life favours 50 % depth of discharge
check: 16.6667 Ah used against 50 % of capacity <= 10 Ah used against 50 % of capacity (83 % depth of discharge per fill at the assumed current; at a 4 A draw a battery rated 20 Ah at the 20 h rate delivers only about 15 to 16 Ah, so nearer 100 %, less in cold weather); to confirm with the pump datasheet, likely a 40 Ah battery with a low-voltage cut-off (proposed, DEC #16)

claim: Fabrication tolerance: the bank serpentine fits inside the lined box with 25 mm at the bends
law: Bend apex at 290 mm from the box centre, lining face at 323 mm; hand-bent tube is typically within a few millimetres
check: 25.06 mm clearance >= 5 mm clearance
closed_by: cad/src/model.py fit checks; cad/fidelity.json (D3, no interference)
